newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia reaches wage pact with Mineworkers Union.
newsitem.headline: Namibia reaches wage pact with Mineworkers Union.

text.p: Namibian national power utility Nampower on Tuesday announced an 11 percent salary increase following talks with the Mine Workers Union of Namibia (MUN) on Monday.
According to a statement released by Nampower, all employees below management level would receive an increase of 11 percent with effect from July 1 1997.

Furthermore the two parties agreed to a joint committee, which would investigate electricity and water subsidies for employees and forward a detailed report to the Nampower board of directors for a decision.
Nampower employees had threatened strike action during a demonstration last Friday if their demands for higher pay and water and electricity subsidies were not met.
This followed protracted negotiations which began in February this year. The MUN lodged a dispute on June 17 when a deadlock in negotiations was registered.
The MUN had demanded a 15 percent salary increase for about 400 union members of the company which employs a total of 782 people, as well as water and electricity subsidies.
Nampower had offered a ten percent salary increase without the subsidies.
